title: The Ultimate FPS Aim Routine (2025 Edition)
author: Aim Pro Coach
excerpt: Stop changing your sensitivity. Here is a simple daily routine to master micro-flicks and tracking.
content:
Aim is the most fundamental skill in competitive FPS games. While game sense is crucial, you cannot execute strategies if you lose your 1v1 duels. In 2025, the mechanical skill ceiling in tactical shooters has skyrocketed because everyone has gotten better at clicking heads.

In this guide, we break down a 30-minute aim routine designed to fix shaky aim, build muscle memory, and help you climb without needing to download heavy software.

The Philosophy: Consistency Over Speed

Many players make the mistake of hopping into a server and trying to flick as fast as possible. This is wrong. Speed is a byproduct of precision. If you watch top-tier aimers like Demon1 or Leo, their crosshair movement looks slow and smooth, but they hit the target instantly because they take the most efficient path.

To achieve this, you need a daily routine. You can use our free online aim trainer right here in your browser to execute this routine before your sessions.

1. The Warmup: Wake Up Your Hand (5 Minutes)

Before jumping into competitive queue, you need to get blood flowing. Start with our Gridshot mode. Do not go for speed yet. Focus on drawing straight lines with your mouse.

  • Goal: Consistently hit targets without over-flicking.
  • Technique: fluid motion. Do not "snap" yet.
  • Why: Cold hands lead to whiffed shots. This 5-minute session activates your fast-twitch muscle fibers.
[Image of hand holding gaming mouse correctly]

2. Mastering Micro-Adjustments (10 Minutes)

Most of your fights in tactical shooters happen within a few centimeters of your crosshair. If you have good crosshair placement, you don't need large flicks; you need micro-adjustments.

Players with strong mechanics rarely need to move their mouse more than an inch to win a duel. To practice this:

  1. Open the Micro Correction exercise on aimtrainerpro.online.
  2. Keep your mouse in the center.
  3. Only click when you are 100% certain of the headshot. Accuracy is more important than KPS (Kills Per Second) here.

3. Tracking and Strafing (10 Minutes)

Tracking is often underrated in tactical shooters. Use the Strafe Track Mode to practice keeping your crosshair on an erratic moving target.

This is also where you practice clean movement timing: change direction, stabilize, then fire a precise shot.

Pro Player Routines

It helps to know what the best in the world are doing. Here is a quick look at how different pros approach their warmup:

Player Focus Style

Demon1 Precision & Tracking Smooth, Low Sens

4. The Cool Down (5 Minutes)

Finish with a high-speed round of Gridshot to test your reaction time limits. Once your arm feels loose and your clicks are crisp, you are ready to rank up.

title: How to Find Your Perfect Sensitivity (PSA Method)
author: Aim Pro Coach
excerpt: Is your sensitivity too high? Learn the PSA Method to calculate your perfect eDPI and see what settings the Pros are using in 2025.
content:
One of the most common questions new players ask is: "What sensitivity should I use?" or "What is TenZ's sens?". Copying a pro player might give you a starting point, but every human has different hand dexterity, reaction times, and mousepad sizes. To truly reach your potential, you need to find your perfect eDPI.

What is eDPI and why does it matter?

eDPI stands for Effective Dots Per Inch. It is the universal standard for measuring sensitivity because it combines your hardware settings with your in-game settings.

The Formula:
Mouse DPI × In-Game Sensitivity = eDPI

Example: 800 DPI × 0.35 Game Sens = 280 eDPI

If you don't know your current eDPI, you can use the built-in settings panel on AimTrainerPro to input your numbers and check your eDPI instantly.

The "PSA Method" (Perfect Sensitivity Approximation)

The PSA method is a scientific way to find your sensitivity by iterating through high and low values. You can do this using an external calculator or manually. Here is how to do it manually in our Training area:

  1. Establish a Baseline: Set your sensitivity so that one full swipe of your mousepad turns you exactly 360 degrees. Let's call this your "Base".
  2. The Bracket: Calculate a "High" sens (Base × 1.5) and a "Low" sens (Base × 0.5).
  3. The Test: Try tracking a target in the Strafe Track mode for 2 minutes with the High sens. Then do 2 minutes with the Low sens.
  4. The Decision: Which one felt better? If Low felt better, that becomes your new baseline. If High felt better, that is your new baseline.
  5. Repeat: Repeat this process 3 or 4 times, narrowing the gap until you find a number that feels perfectly natural.

If you want a tool to do the math for you, the PSA Method Calculator is a great external resource to keep open in another tab while you train.

Example Pro Settings (2025 Updated)

Most top-ranked players fall into the eDPI range of 160 to 400. Anything higher is usually considered "wrist aiming" (risky for consistency), and anything lower is "arm aiming" (great for precision but tiring).

Player DPI Sens eDPI
Demon1 1600 0.10 160
TenZ 800 ~0.35 280
Aspas 800 0.40 320
f0rsakeN 800 0.712 569 (High!)

As you can see, Demon1 plays on an incredibly low sensitivity (160 eDPI), which allows for pixel-perfect micro-adjustments but requires large arm movements. f0rsakeN, on the other hand, is a wrist aimer with very high sensitivity.

Tools to Convert Sensitivity

If you are coming from other games, you shouldn't guess your sensitivity. Use a sensitivity converter to maintain muscle memory between titles.

For conversions, you can use sites like Mouse-Sensitivity.com or Aiming.Pro Calculator.

Conclusion

There is no "magic number." The best sensitivity is the one that allows you to track a target smoothly without jittering. Use our aim trainer to test different eDPI settings today. Start with 280 eDPI (800 DPI x 0.35) and adjust from there using the PSA method.

title: How to Improve Aim in FPS Games (Beginner to Pro Guide)
author: Aim Pro Coach
excerpt: A complete step-by-step plan to improve aim in any FPS game with drills, settings, and a practical weekly routine.
content:
Most players try to improve aim by grinding ranked matches. The problem is that ranked games do not give enough focused reps. If you want faster progress, you need deliberate practice: clear drills, measurable goals, and stable settings.

This guide gives you a practical framework used by strong FPS players across Valorant, CS2, and Fortnite. You can run every drill in our free browser aim trainer and track your consistency over time.

Why Aim Improvement Feels Slow

Aim feels random when your training is random. Common mistakes include changing sensitivity every few days, doing only speed drills, and skipping warmups. Good aim is a compound skill built from three parts:

  • Crosshair placement: pre-aim likely angles before fights.
  • Mouse control: smooth and precise hand movement.
  • Click timing: shoot only when your crosshair is on target.

The 4 Drill Categories You Need

Use all four categories each week. Relying on one type of drill creates gaps in mechanics.

1) Static Clicking

Static targets improve pure precision and first-shot accuracy. Prioritize clean lines over raw speed.

2) Dynamic Clicking (Flicks)

Targets appear in different positions and force quick directional changes. This builds confidence in surprise duels.

3) Tracking

Follow moving targets with smooth control. Tracking matters in nearly every game, even tactical shooters.

4) Micro-Adjustments

Small corrections around the head area are often the difference between a hit and a miss.

Daily Routine (30 Minutes)

  1. 5 min warmup: easy static targets, focus on relaxed grip.
  2. 8 min flicks: medium tempo, emphasize stopping power.
  3. 8 min tracking: smooth pathing with minimal jitter.
  4. 6 min micro-corrections: tiny target precision.
  5. 3 min benchmark run: one score-focused attempt.

Settings That Actually Matter

Keep these stable for at least 2 weeks:

  • DPI: 400, 800, or 1600 (most common pro ranges).
  • In-game sensitivity: choose a value you can control comfortably.
  • Mouse acceleration: off for consistency.
  • Polling rate: 1000Hz if your mouse supports it.

Need help tuning sensitivity? Read How to Find Your Perfect Sensitivity.

Weekly Progress Tracking

Measure progress with the same scenarios and settings each week. Use three numbers:

  • Accuracy %
  • Targets hit per minute
  • Best score and 7-day average

If your average goes up slowly, your aim is improving even if your best score is unchanged.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

  • Training only when you feel motivated.
  • Copying a pro setup without testing control.
  • Ignoring posture and arm tension.
  • Spamming shots instead of confirming crosshair placement.

Conclusion

Aim improvement is not luck. Build a repeatable routine, keep settings stable, and track your averages. If you train with intent for 4 to 6 weeks, your in-game confidence and duel win rate will climb.

title: Flick Aim vs Tracking Aim: What's the Difference?
author: Aim Pro Coach
excerpt: Understand when to use flicking vs tracking, how to train each skill, and why most players need both to rank up.
content:
Players often ask whether they should train flicking or tracking. The short answer: both. They solve different problems in combat and improve different parts of your mechanics.

What Is Flick Aim?

Flicking is moving your crosshair rapidly from one point to another, then firing. It is common in tactical shooters when enemies swing angles or when you clear multiple threats quickly.

  • Best for first-shot bursts and headshot duels.
  • Relies on stopping precision and click timing.
  • Punishes over-flicking and rushed shots.

What Is Tracking Aim?

Tracking is keeping your crosshair on a moving target over time. It is critical in games with continuous movement and automatic weapons.

  • Best for sustained damage on moving targets.
  • Relies on smooth control and prediction.
  • Punishes tension and jittery mouse movement.

Which One Matters More?

In Valorant and CS2, flicking and micro-corrections usually matter more in final duel outcomes. In Fortnite and fast arena shooters, tracking has larger impact. Most players should train a balanced split and then bias toward their main game.

Training Split Recommendation

  1. Tactical shooter focus: 60% flicking, 40% tracking.
  2. Movement-heavy shooter focus: 40% flicking, 60% tracking.

Drills You Can Use Today

In our online aim trainer, run:

  • Static and dynamic click scenarios for flicking.
  • Strafe tracking scenarios for tracking control.
  • Small target mode for micro-adjustment transfer.

Big Mistakes

  • Only doing fast flick drills with poor accuracy.
  • Ignoring tracking because your game is "tactical".
  • Changing sensitivity every time scores dip.

Conclusion

Flicking wins sudden duels. Tracking wins moving duels. Train both with intention and your mechanics will become more complete. Read next: Best DPI Settings for FPS Games.

title: Best Sensitivity Settings for Valorant (Pro Player Guide)
author: Valorant Coach
excerpt: Learn how to choose a stable Valorant sensitivity using DPI, eDPI ranges, and practical in-game testing.
content:
Choosing sensitivity in Valorant should be a process, not a guess. You want a setting that supports clean head-level micro-corrections without sacrificing turn speed.

Core Terms

  • DPI: mouse hardware sensitivity.
  • In-game sens: Valorant sensitivity slider value.
  • eDPI: DPI multiplied by in-game sens.

Practical eDPI Range

Many competitive players cluster between roughly 160 and 400 eDPI. Lower values can improve precision but require larger arm movement. Higher values can feel faster but often reduce consistency on tiny corrections.

Simple Test Method

  1. Pick a starting eDPI around 250 to 320.
  2. Run 10 minutes of micro and flick drills in our trainer.
  3. Rate control from 1 to 10.
  4. Adjust by small steps only (5% to 10%).
  5. Lock settings for 14 days.

When to Lower Sensitivity

  • You frequently overflick short angles.
  • Your crosshair jitters at long range.

When to Raise Sensitivity

  • You cannot track quick close-range swings.
  • You feel physically limited by pad space.

Conclusion

There is no universal best sensitivity, only a value you can repeat under pressure. Test, track, and commit. Read next: How to Find Your Perfect Sensitivity.

What Makes a Good Crosshair

  • Strong contrast against bright and dark backgrounds.
  • Simple shape that does not block head hitboxes.
  • Stable center point for micro-corrections.

Recommended Starting Style

Use a minimal static crosshair with outlines enabled if visibility is a problem. Keep movement and firing error off unless you intentionally use them as feedback tools.

Testing Method

  1. Pick two crosshair variants only.
  2. Run 10 minutes in our aim trainer.
  3. Play 3 ranked games each.
  4. Keep the one with better confidence and clearer first-shot reads.

Color Suggestions

Cyan, green, and white are popular for visibility. Map lighting can affect preference, so test on maps where you play most often.

Conclusion

Crosshair settings should reduce noise, not create it. Choose clarity, keep it consistent, and build muscle memory around one setup. Read next: Best Aim Training for Valorant Players.

title: Best DPI Settings for FPS Games
author: FPS Training Team
excerpt: A clear DPI guide for FPS players, including common pro ranges, myths, and setup recommendations.
content:
DPI is one of the most misunderstood aim settings. Many players think higher DPI means better aim, but DPI alone does not decide performance. Your full sensitivity chain matters.

What DPI Actually Does

DPI controls how far the cursor moves per inch of mouse movement. In FPS games, effective sensitivity depends on DPI and in-game sensitivity together.

Common Competitive DPI Choices

  • 400 DPI: classic and controlled.
  • 800 DPI: widely used and flexible.
  • 1600 DPI: common with lower in-game sens values.

Simple Recommendation

Choose 800 DPI if you want an easy baseline, then tune in-game sensitivity gradually. Avoid switching DPI daily.

Testing in Practice

Run flick and tracking scenarios in our browser aim trainer. If aim feels jittery, lower overall sensitivity. If you cannot keep up in close fights, raise it slightly.

Conclusion

The best DPI setting is the one that supports stable control and repeatable mechanics. Keep your setup simple and consistent. Read next: Low Sens vs High Sens.

title: Low Sens vs High Sens: Which Is Better for Aim?
author: FPS Training Team
excerpt: Compare low and high sensitivity playstyles, pros and cons, and how to choose the right setup for your game.
content:
The low-sens vs high-sens debate has no universal winner. Your ideal setup depends on your game, mouse space, and control style.

Low Sens Advantages

  • Better micro-precision at long range.
  • More stable first-shot control.
  • Often easier for tactical shooter consistency.

Low Sens Drawbacks

  • More arm movement and fatigue.
  • Harder fast turns in close fights.

High Sens Advantages

  • Fast directional changes.
  • Easier close-range reaction play.

High Sens Drawbacks

  • More jitter risk on fine corrections.
  • Can punish overflick habits.

How to Decide

  1. Run both styles for one week each.
  2. Track average accuracy and duel confidence.
  3. Choose the style that feels repeatable under stress.

Use our free aim trainer online to test both setups in identical drills.

Conclusion

Pick the sensitivity style that supports consistency, not just occasional highlight clips. Read next: Best Aim Training Routine.
